_comment: How a pal GROWS and how its worth is read. ALL of it is TUNABLE and none of it is a mechanic. The expected feedback is 'levelling takes forever', 'a level-up doesn't feel like anything happened', 'every pal I catch appraises the same', 'I never see a rare trait' — every one of those has to be answerable by editing this file rather than by editing code.
_comment_firewall: What a TRAIT is — its name, its description, what it multiplies — lives in data/traits/traits.json. This file may only say how OFTEN one is rolled. If a value here could change what a trait DOES, it is in the wrong file.
_comment_capacity: The five-pal limit is NOT in this file, and its absence is the point. CLAUDE.md makes it a hard rule twice over ('Player can own only five pals total', 'Never implement pal storage beyond five'), so it is a const in scripts/pals/party.gd where it cannot be turned by editing data. Nothing here should ever be able to make room for a sixth.

levels._comment: GAME_DESIGN.md 11 fixes the range at 1-50. The cap is therefore closer to design than to tuning, but it lives here because the Meadows slice will never approach it and a lower cap is the obvious lever if levelling in one biome outruns the content.

xp._comment: XP needed to leave a level: `base * level^exponent`, rounded. Progress resets to zero at each level rather than accumulating a lifetime total, so `xp_for_next_level()` is the only number a bar ever has to divide by. Combat is the primary source (GAME_DESIGN.md 11); nothing awards XP yet, so these are a shape rather than a balance.
xp._comment_exponent: Above 1 so later levels cost more, low enough that level 20 is not a wall. At 1.55 the first level costs 60 and the tenth costs about 2100 — roughly the curve of an afternoon's fights rather than a season's.

growth._comment: Fraction of the species base stat added per level, LINEARLY: `base * (1 + per_level * (level - 1))`. Not compounding. A 9%-per-level compound reaches 74x by level 50 and turns every fight into either a walkover or a wall; linear reaches about 5x, which keeps a low-level pal usable and a high-level one clearly better.
growth._comment_hp_leads: HP grows fastest on purpose. Attack and defence both feed the same bounded damage formula in combat_math.base_damage, so raising them together barely moves time-to-kill; HP is the stat that actually makes a levelled pal survive a fight it used to lose.

appraisal._comment: How this individual's stats are turned into stars. GAME_DESIGN.md 11: 'show appraisal through stars/bars, not exact IV numbers'. scripts/pals/pal_instance.gd `appraisal()` returns the raw ratios AND the star count; the UI is expected to draw the stars and may draw the bars, but must not print the ratios.
appraisal._comment_bands: Ascending thresholds on `stat / species baseline at this level`. A pal clears one star to begin with and gains one for each band it passes, so four bands give five stars. Tight around 1.0 because the trait modifiers in data/traits/traits.json only span about 0.86-1.18 — wider bands would make every pal a three.

trait_roll._comment: Relative likelihood of each trait when a pal is created. Keys are trait ids from data/traits/traits.json. Weights are relative, not percentages, so a new trait can be added without renormalising the rest.
trait_roll._comment_default: Any trait present in traits.json but missing from `weights` is rolled at this weight rather than never appearing. A trait that is invisible because someone forgot a line here is the kind of bug that is only found by not finding a trait.
trait_roll._comment_steady: Steady is the boring one and is weighted to be the most common. The strong traits only feel strong because most pals do not have one.
